comment: The same failure happens in full identity systems, because a template built for one language quietly governs every layout decision that follows it. Designing the Arabic version first, on its own grid, is what reveals whether the brand actually has a system or only a Latin logo with translations attached.

Nice observation. The stall has one advantage most brand palettes don't: every color is there because of what sells, so nothing is decoration. Does that kind of market reference end up in your client mood boards?
Clear hierarchy is what makes a brand readable in seconds. Was that the goal from the start?
